title: S1 V3.9 Macro and session context
question: Do Macro WAIT and entry session justify hard S1 entry restrictions under the current V3.9 trade export?
hypothesis: They may change expectancy, but should not be assumed to be binary permissions without V3.9 evidence.

findings.title: Macro WAIT remained profitable
findings.detail: 211 matched trades; WR 56.87%, PF 1.837. The evidence does not support a categorical S1 block.

findings.title: Asia was not the weak V3.9 session
findings.detail: 154 trades; WR 57.79%, PF 1.999. The inherited Asia-only observation rule is not supported.

findings.title: Session effects are context, not causality
findings.detail: Confidence intervals overlap and subgroup composition may differ. Apply shrunk score adjustments, not optimized gates.

policy_impacts.summary: Macro and session adjust the S1 recommendation score and cannot create or cancel a signal.
V3.9 subgroup evidence replaces the older V3.4-derived Macro hard block.
Clock time is descriptive context rather than an entry prohibition.
